hero.pill: A live dashboard page you can talk to
hero.title: A face for your agent
hero.lead: A private dashboard page your agent can launch and reshape live as your requests change. Talk to it, share device sensors, store real shared database state, and invite others in.
hero.sub: It’s like giving your agent **eyes, ears, and a form of expression** — on your phone, laptop, or tablet.

start.eyebrow: Works with the agent you already use
start.title: Point it at {host}. Tell it what you want.
start.p1: Take your **Claude Code**, **Codex**, **Meta Muse**, **Instinct**, **OpenAI Dots**, **Claude Duet**, **GrokBot**, **OpenClaw**, or **Hermes** — point it at **{host}**, describe the page you want, and give it the email to tie it to.
start.p2: It hands back a private URL. Open it from your phone, laptop, or tablet, sign in with **GitHub** or **Google**, and you’re connected. Invite family or teammates anytime with a private link.
start.promptHint: Swap in your own email and idea

start.platformsLead: Pick your harness for a quick start — click a platform for the human guide, or `.md` for the AI-friendly page.

pillars.title: A dashboard you can talk to — that changes with your requests.
pillars.lead: Chat threads are great for words, not for looking inside your fridge, querying a shared database across phones, or inviting your team into a live view that adapts on the fly.

items.title: Talk to it, reshape it live
items.body: Ask by voice or text and watch your agent evolve the page itself — adding charts, rearranging buttons, showing annotated diagrams, or reading next steps aloud as your work shifts.

items.title: Eyes & ears on your terms
items.body: Let your agent see through your phone camera, hear voice notes, track GPS and motion, view a shared screen, or read connected USB, Serial, Bluetooth, and MIDI hardware — only when you allow it.

items.title: Real shared database state
items.body: Not ephemeral chat memory — a genuine local-first SQL and event database (Chronolog) synced peer-to-peer across your devices and your agent, so reads and edits keep working even offline.

items.title: Invite others in
items.body: Share a private guest invite link — open or locked to a specific email — or a display-only link. Collaborators sign in via GitHub or Google and share the same live dashboard, database, and agent.

how.title: From one message to a live connected app.
how.lead: No servers to provision, no app-store review, no auth boilerplate to wire up. Your agent builds the page; you own the keys and invite whoever you want.

steps.title: Point your agent here
steps.body: Give your agent your idea, **{host}**, and the email you’ll use to sign in.

steps.title: It builds & publishes
steps.body: Your agent sets up the shared database, builds the browser UI, and publishes a signed release.

steps.title: Open & sign in
steps.body: Tap the URL on your phone, laptop, or tablet and log in with GitHub or Google.

steps.title: Talk, invite & evolve
steps.body: Share sensors, invite others, and ask your agent to reshape the dashboard anytime.

how.note: **How the pieces fit:** Shared data belongs to your app’s **Chronolog** session, saved locally so ordinary reads and edits keep working even offline. Tendriller hosts the signed page and access controls; live agent reactions run whenever your agent’s connected process is active.

ideas.title: Whatever fits the moment.
ideas.lead: Spin up a quick helper for an afternoon repair or a permanent shared dashboard your family or team keeps on their Home Screen.

items.title: Kitchen companion
items.body: Look inside the fridge with your phone, share a live shopping database with your household, and follow spoken recipe steps hands-free.

items.title: Living team tracker
items.body: Invite teammates into a shared SQL dashboard for tasks, inventory, or budgets — and ask your agent to add new views and charts live.

items.title: Hands-on repair helper
items.body: Point your phone at a bike, car, or wiring job while your agent highlights parts, shows diagrams, and walks through next steps.

items.title: Shared field notebook
items.body: Collect photos, location pins, and voice memos on a walk while your agent organizes everyone’s observations into a live map and log.

items.title: Outdoor & sports companion
items.body: Build your own custom deck for sailing, cycling, geocaching, or trail checklists driven by live GPS and motion sensors.

items.title: Workshop instrument
items.body: Connect a Bluetooth, Serial, USB, or MIDI device straight from the browser and let your agent chart and interpret live readings.

items.title: Multi-device workspace
items.body: Use your phone as a handheld camera or barcode scanner while your computer displays the full interactive office dashboard.

items.title: Collaborative sketchpad
items.body: Draw, annotate, and vote on ideas with invited guests while your agent reshapes the controls, palettes, and layout in real time.

items.title: Screen & accessibility copilot
items.body: Share a window for guided troubleshooting, or wire up a gamepad or assistive switch to trigger custom page actions.

access.title: Private by default. Always on your terms.
access.lead: Giving your agent a face — and inviting others in — shouldn’t mean handing over your accounts or leaving a mic open behind your back.

items.title: End-to-end encrypted
items.body: All application data, shared database records, and live peer streams are encrypted end-to-end with keys that stay on your devices. Tendriller has zero insight into your content — even when relaying traffic.

items.title: GitHub or Google sign-in
items.body: Your page is private by default and gated by OAuth login. Invited guests sign in with their own account; your agent never sees your credentials.

items.title: Revocable agent & guest access
items.body: Agents hold separate scoped keys and guest invites can be locked to an email or revoked anytime from your dashboard.

items.title: Device-level sensor prompts
items.body: Camera, microphone, location, screen, and hardware access are always requested explicitly on the device where you open the page.

access.openSourceNote: **Open source & self-hostable:** Don’t want to trust our hosted server? Every piece of Tendriller is open source on GitHub — inspect the code, run your own instance locally with `npm run dev`, or deploy it on your own Cloudflare account.

namesake.body: An agent can extend its tendrils into other devices’ interfaces and sensors. Tendriller makes the opening for each new connection, like a drill.

platforms.indexLead: Every platform below has both a human getting-started guide and a plain Markdown page your agent can read directly at `{host}`.

claude-code.summary: Runs in your terminal with shell access, Node 24, and optional MCP — ideal for building, publishing, and evolving a live Tendriller page directly.
claude-code.prompt: Read {base}/docs/BUILD_AN_APP.md and build me a live Tendriller dashboard tied to you@example.com — give it a shared SQL database for our project tasks, let me invite teammates, and let me talk to the page to reshape views and controls.
steps: Open Claude Code in a fresh folder (with Node 24 installed) and paste the prompt pointing at {host} and your email.
Claude Code checks readiness, downloads the verified starter kit, creates your page, and publishes a signed release.
Open the private URL it hands back on your phone, laptop, or tablet, sign in with GitHub or Google, and ask Claude Code to modify the page live anytime.

codex.summary: Builds and deploys a full local-first Tendriller workspace straight from your shell or Codex app, with optional account-linked MCP support.
codex.prompt: Follow {base}/docs/BUILD_AN_APP.md and launch a Tendriller page tied to you@example.com — include a shared SQL database, camera capture, and a voice-enabled dashboard I can reshape with new requests.
steps: Start Codex in a workspace directory (with Node 24 available) and send the prompt referencing {host} and your email.
Codex verifies host readiness, installs the exact release kit, initializes your page, and publishes the signed browser interface.
Tap the returned URL on any device, sign in via GitHub or Google, and keep iterating with Codex as your requirements change.

meta-muse.summary: Give Meta Muse eyes, ears, and a live shared canvas across your phone, tablet, and desktop.
meta-muse.prompt: Go to {base} and launch a live Tendriller page tied to you@example.com — build a kitchen and household companion with a shared shopping database I can invite my partner to, fridge camera snapshots, and hands-free voice steps.
steps: Tell Meta Muse what kind of live page you want, point it at {host}, and include the email you’ll use to sign in.
Meta Muse reads the onboarding guide at {host}/agent.md, creates the page, and returns a private URL.
Open the URL on your phone, laptop, or tablet, sign in with GitHub or Google, and grant whichever sensors you want it to use.

instinct.summary: Connect Instinct to a live browser dashboard with camera, voice, location, and shared database state.
instinct.prompt: Point to {base} and create a live Tendriller dashboard tied to you@example.com — let me talk to it on my phone, track field observations with GPS and photos in a shared database, and reshape the layout as I ask.
steps: Send Instinct a message describing your page, referencing {host} and your sign-in email.
Instinct follows the machine-readable guide to create and publish your signed page and hands you the URL.
Open the link on any device, sign in with GitHub or Google, and share guest invite links whenever you want others to join.

openai-dots.summary: Pair OpenAI Dots with a live multi-device Tendriller page you can talk to, share with others, and reshape on demand.
openai-dots.prompt: Use {base} to build a private Tendriller page tied to you@example.com — a live dashboard I can talk to, backed by a shared SQL database, with guest invites so my team can collaborate in real time.
steps: Point OpenAI Dots at {host} (or connect via Tendriller’s MCP endpoint at {host}/mcp) and describe the dashboard you want plus your email.
It prepares the shared state and publishes a signed browser interface, then returns your private page URL.
Open the URL on your phone, laptop, or tablet and sign in with GitHub or Google to connect.

claude-duet.summary: Turn Claude Duet into a visual, voice-ready collaborator with a live dashboard that evolves with every request.
claude-duet.prompt: Read {base}/agent.md and create a Tendriller dashboard tied to you@example.com — make a collaborative workspace with shared database state, a live sketchpad, and voice controls I can reshape as we work.
steps: Tell Claude Duet what you want to collaborate on, point it to {host}, and include your email address.
Claude Duet follows the Tendriller guide to build the interface, define shared state, and publish a signed URL.
Sign in via GitHub or Google from your phone, tablet, or laptop — and invite others with a private link when ready.

grokbot.summary: Give GrokBot a live browser face with camera input, voice interaction, and persistent shared state across your devices.
grokbot.prompt: Go to {base} and spin up a live Tendriller page tied to you@example.com — let me point my phone camera at what I’m working on, ask questions out loud, and keep a shared log I can check from my laptop.
steps: Give GrokBot your task, {host}, and the email you’ll use to sign in.
GrokBot reads {host}/agent.md, creates and publishes your signed Tendriller page, and sends back the URL.
Open the link on any device, sign in with GitHub or Google, and enable camera or microphone permissions on demand.

openclaw.summary: Pair your self-hosted OpenClaw agent with a private, signed multi-device web face, sensors, and shared SQL state.
openclaw.prompt: Read {base}/docs/BUILD_AN_APP.md and set up a Tendriller workspace tied to you@example.com — launch a live control dashboard with shared SQL state, voice input, and hardware sensor support that I can open from my phone.
steps: Point your OpenClaw agent at {host} with your goal and your sign-in email (or keep one Tendriller workspace for many pages).
OpenClaw registers once, creates and publishes a signed page, and can keep `tendril agent run` online for live reactions.
Open the URL on your phone or laptop, sign in with GitHub or Google, and pin the page to your Home Screen.

hermes.summary: Give Hermes a live, revocable browser interface for sensors, voice prompts, shared databases, and real-time human collaboration.
hermes.prompt: Read {base}/agent.md and launch a Tendriller page tied to you@example.com — build a live dashboard I can talk to, store structured records in a shared SQL database, and let me invite collaborators.
steps: Give Hermes your request, point it to {host}, and include the email address to tie the page to.
Hermes verifies readiness, publishes the signed browser app, and returns the private URL.
Open the URL on any device, sign in with GitHub or Google, and ask Hermes to adapt the interface as your work evolves.
